name: path_sanitize
title: Sanitize a filename by removing directory paths and invalid characters

origin.description:
path_sanitize() removes the following:

- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C0_and_C1_control_codesControl characters
- https://web.archive.org/web/20230126161942/https://kb.acronis.com/content/39790Reserved characters
- Unix reserved filenames (. and ..)
- Trailing periods and spaces (invalid on Windows)
- Windows reserved filenames (CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1, COM2,
COM3, COM4, COM5, COM6, COM7, COM8, COM9, LPT1, LPT2,
LPT3, LPT4, LPT5, LPT6, LPT7, LPT8, and LPT9)
The resulting string is then truncated to https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comparison_of_file_systems#Limits255 bytes in length

arguments.name: filename
arguments.text: A character vector to be sanitized.

arguments.name: replacement
arguments.text: A character vector used to replace invalid characters.

origin.example:
# potentially unsafe string
str <- "~/.\u0001ssh/authorized_keys"
path_sanitize(str)

path_sanitize("..")
